title: Meet Trebbiano
subtitle: Neutral, crisp and prolific
objectives: Explain why it's so widely planted

steps.title: Light and neutral
steps.body: Trebbiano, called Ugni Blanc in France, gives light, crisp whites with lemon, green apple, almond and herbs. It has high acidity and moderate alcohol, and is fairly neutral in aroma. It's one of the most planted white grapes in the world, mostly for brandy and simple wines.

steps.title: Why so widespread
steps.body: Trebbiano is vigorous, productive and resistant to disease, and keeps high acidity even when yields are high. That makes it ideal for distillation, where neutral, acidic, low-alcohol wine is needed. Its many clones and relatives, like Trebbiano Toscano and Trebbiano Romagnolo, share the family name.

steps.prompt: Why is Trebbiano valued for brandy?
options: It gives neutral, acidic, low-alcohol wine
steps.explanation: Distillers want neutral, acidic base wine.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: As a still wine, Trebbiano is pale, light, crisp and neutral, with lemon and almond. It's often blended to add freshness. Trebbiano d'Abruzzo, a distinct variety, can be more serious, especially from top producers like Valentini.

steps.prompt: Trebbiano is a low-yielding, delicate grape.
steps.explanation: Not true. It's vigorous and productive.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Trebbiano gives light, crisp, neutral whites
It's productive and keeps high acidity
It's one of the most planted white grapes
